sections.html:
• Scientific name: Hypostomus aff. pusarum
  • Common names: L078, Parnaiba Pleco
  • Etymology: Greek, hypo = under + Greek, stoma = mouth.
  • IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated

• Diet: omnivore
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (2022)

The Hypostomus genus has 7 soft rays in the dorsal fin, whereas the similar-looking Pterygoplichthys species have 10 soft dorsal fin rays.
Brazil, Maranhão, Rio Parnaiba drainage, Piauí Rivers, Parnaíba.
South America: middle Rio Parnaíba basin and northeastern coastal drainages of Brazil. Type locality: Ceará Mirim, Brazil.
As with most of this genus, it will do well in a larger aquarium, although this is one of the smaller species in the genus. The aquarium should be well filtered.
Water parameters can be quite diverse for this genus. Temperature 22-25°C, pH 6.5-7.2.
Omnivore with a liking for green foods, tablet foods and frozen foods.
Breeding: unreported. There is no breeding report.

Etymology: the specific name pusarum has the commemorative suffix -arum (Latin, plural), in memory of the boys who collected this catfish with their hands and with dip-nets under overhanging grassy banks at Ceará-Mirim, Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil, "the best collectors we found in Brazil" (presumably based on a native word, meaning unknown).

IUCN: Hypostomus pusarum occurs in the coastal basins of Rio Grande do Norte and Paraíba, northeastern Brazil. It is a frequent, abundant species and no threats that compromise its population have been identified. It was categorised as Least Concern (IUCN 2022).
